text:
**For the safest bet, get the Jackery HomePower 3000.** It has enough capacity for a full night even under a high-use estimate: one sizing guide estimates a queen blanket at 260 W and says about 2,600 Wh is needed for eight hours; it lists the HomePower 3000 at roughly 9.5 hours. ([estimate and runtime](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/))

If your blanket is lower-wattage or you’ll use a low setting, a **1 kWh station** may be enough: the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is listed at 1,024 Wh, with an estimated 12 hours for a 150 W blanket that cycles on and off. ([BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 estimate](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket))

**Check the blanket’s wattage label before buying.** Runtime varies a lot with its draw and thermostat cycling; one guide estimates a 100 W blanket uses about 1 kWh for eight hours. ([runtime guide](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/))
